plain_english: Your duties depend on your relationships. Is someone your father? Then you need to take care of him, listen to him, and put up with his criticism and correction. But what if he's a bad father? Your natural bond isn't to a good father — it's to a father, period. Is your brother unfair? Then keep being fair to him yourself. Don't focus on what he does. Focus on what you need to do to keep your own character in line with nature. No one can hurt you unless you let them. You only get hurt when you choose to be hurt. Practice this way of thinking. Look at your relationships — neighbor, citizen, soldier — and you'll know what duties each one requires.
original_excerpt: Duties are universally measured by relations. Is a certain man your father? In this are implied taking care of him, submitting to him in all things, patiently receiving his reproaches, his correction. But he is a bad father. Is your natural tie, then, to a _good_ father? No, but to a father. Is a brother unjust? Well, preserve your own just relation toward him. Consider not what _he_ does, but what _you_ are to do to keep your own will in a state conformable to nature, for another cannot hurt you unless you please. You will then be hurt when you consent to be hurt. In this manner, therefore, if you accustom yourself to contemplate the relations of neighbor, citizen, commander, you can deduce from each the corresponding duties.
